title: LOUISVILLE FALL HARVEST FESTIVAL
full_story:
The 75th Annual Louisville Fall Harvest Festival starts this afternoon when the Kiddie Parade kicks things off at 2 pm.

Full Armor Christian School will be serving treats at the old Soda Fountain, and the Red Brush Christian Church will be serving apple cider and the Louisville Christian Church will be serving free water near the pocket park.  From 4 to 6 pm the Methodist Church will be offering free chili with Das-zle Dance and tumble performing at 5:30 pm.  From 5:30 to 6:30 pm will be the past Queen reception at the State Bank Suite.  At 6:15 pm Sylvia and Meila Robey will sing on stage.  The Little Miss, JR Miss, and Queen pageants will be held at 7:00 pm.  There are 6 contestants vying for the title of Louisville Fall Festival Queen, The current Queen is Mila Zink.  There are 7 contestants in the JR Miss contest, the current JR Miss is Elsie Anderson, and there are 10 young ladies vying for the Little Miss title held by Landrey Eade.

The glow 5K Walk, Run will take place after the pageants.  From 9 to 10 pm there will be music on the square with Seth Schnautz.

Tomorrow the festival will start with the Rotary Pancake breakfast from 7 to Noon.  The FFA, AG Mechanics Tractor show will be on the east side of the square and kids activities will start at 8 am and the Clay County Genealogical Society Library will have an open house.  The Clay County Cruisers Car Show begins at 9, there will also be a greased pig contest, sponsored by the Hoosier Prairie Baptist Church, and a country store will open at the old Clay County Jail with free coffee and popcorn.

The Princess pageant will be on the main stage at 10 am with special guest Briley Mullins performing.  Starting at 11 am will be the Chili Cook Off Contest, hosted by the North Clay FCCLA and the Louisville Chamber of Commerce, with tastings available to 1 pm.  Contestants should bring their chili to the pocket park by 10:45 am.  The winner will get a $50 prize.  At 11:30 am Power and Grace Tumbling will perform on the main stage.  At 1 pm Deputy Trevin Smith and his K9 Chief will have a demonstration.  The parade is at 2 pm, Katrina Van Dyke has been named as the parade marshal.  Following the parade the crowning of the Queens and the Rotary Basket Raffle winners will be announced.

For the Parade floats, cars, tractors, bands and Queens will line up at the grade school, horses will line up at the city park, Louisville Queens and contestants will line up on Magnolia Street, and Emergency Services will line up at the high school.  Handicap parking for the parade will be available on the east side of the square.

All weekend there will be arts, and crafts, food vendors, basket raffle and inflatables for the kids.

In conjunction with the Fall Harvest Festival the Louisville American Legion will have a meat shoot on Sunday, November 1st at 11 am.

title: FLORA HALLOWEEN PARADE
full_story:
The Flora Chamber of Commerce Halloween Parade is tomorrow night, at 7:00 pm.  All entries to the parade must be registered with the Chamber in order to participate.  Unfortunately, Executive Director, Arriel Dulaney, has been unable to be in the office over the last few days due to circumstances beyond anyone’s control.  If you haven’t already registered, please feel free to register online from the chamber website or print off a copy of the registration form fill it out, and leave it in the Chamber’s mailbox at the Depot Building.  If you have any questions, please feel free to send the Chamber a message or call the Chamber’s at 618-662-5646.

The parade route will start at The Depot (State Street) and end at Christ Church (Olive Street).  Emergency vehicles will be allowed to sound their sirens during the parade.

Staging areas will be given the day you register and parade numbers will be given the day of the parade when you check in.  Location of your Staging Area will be based on the type of entry.  The Chamber is asking everyone to please be respectful of the staging areas and leave them in the same condition they were in upon arrival.  All entries must check in with the staging area volunteer in the brightly colored vest, to officially check in and verify the entry has their card number on their entry for judging.  Bands, queens, and political entries do not need parade cards but do need to check in with the stage volunteer.

Horses are to unload at the Price Less IGA at 6 pm with a mandatory police escort to the grass area of GSI beginning at 6:15 pm.  If you miss the police escort you will not be permitted in the parade.

Handicap spectators may park at Southern Lumber Company (corner of E. North Ave & South Mill) and please use the south entrance closest to the tracks.

All entries are required to register.  A $10 late fee will be required by any unregistered participant if they register after Noon tomorrow.  There will be absolutely no throwing of candy from vehicles or trailers/float, candy can be handed out or tossed if you are a walker on the sides of the street.  If an entry is caught throwing, they will be disqualified from judging.

Performance groups may stop at the judging stand and do a performance no longer than 90 seconds.  Any performance longer than 90 seconds will disqualify you from judging.

title: DAYLIGHT SAVING TIME ENDS
full_story:
Millions of Americans will turn back their clocks tomorrow night, before going to bed, marking the end of Daylight-Saving Time in 2026.

The controversial practice of “springing forward” and “falling back” has been observed in most states for decades.  Under the current Daylight-Saving Time period, most Americans lose an hour of sleep on the second Sunday of March and gain an hour the first Sunday of November.

Daylight Saving Time ends Sunday, November 1st at 2 am.  We will “fall back,” turning our clocks back to 1 am, gaining an extra hour of sleep.

As the clock turns back an hour on that weekend, it’s also a good time to check your smoke detectors and make sure you have a fire escape plan that allows all family members to get out in two minutes if a fire occurs.

In 2005 Daylight Saving Time was shifted to begin on the second Sunday of March and end on the first Sunday of November.  A Department of Energy study found the extra daylight saves around 0.5% in total electricity daily in the US, equaling energy savings of 1.3 billion kilowatt-hours annually.

Next year, Daylight saving time will begin on Sunday, March 14th.

title: NOBLE VILLAGE BOARD
full_story:
The Noble Village Board met Monday night to map out a busy holiday calendar and tackle key village business.

Board members received updates regarding sexual harassment informational resources and the Richland County Recreation Commission.  They also agreed to schedule an upcoming Personnel Committee meeting and shared progress on the installation of the new, ADA accessible swing for the park.  Officials noted that the upcoming tax levy details should be ready for review by the next scheduled meeting.  In new business, trustees made the call to cancel the second regular board meeting in December to accommodate the holidays.  Village employees will celebrate their annual Christmas party at Joe’s Pizza on December 10th at 6:00 pm.

Residents were reminded that The Noble Lions Club is hosting their annual Pancake Breakfast on Saturday, November 14th, from 7:00 to 11:00 am and the Christmas Parade will be on November 28th at 6 pm.

title: LEAF COLLECTION UNDERWAY
full_story:
The City of Flora Department of Public Works fall curbside leaf collection will begin Sunday.  City residents should have their loose leaves to the curbside on their normal scheduled leaf collection day.  Please keep in mind that the crew may run behind schedule during this time, and they appreciate your patience and understanding.  To help crews more efficiently collect leaves, please remember the following, rake leaves in wind rows, a long narrow line, rather than piles next to the curb.  Also, the City will not pick up anything in the alley.

Keep wind rows as close to the curb as possible but do not rake leaves into the street.  This is in violation of a city ordinance and will plug the storm sewers.

Keep wind rows away from trees, hydrants, signposts, electrical pedestals, or other obstacles.

Keep all garbage, metal, branches, and sticks out of the wind rows.

Do not park vehicles next to the leaf wind rows.  If they can’t get the vacuum to the wind rows, they will have to wait until your next collection day.

As a reminder this is a 2-person operation so wind rows must be narrow & close to the curb.  Bulky limbs and cuttings from trees and shrubs must be cut into four-foot lengths and tied into bundles not more than two feet in diameter.  Wood and brush should not be placed in a container or garbage can.  Please place this directly on the curb.  All property owners are responsible for disposing of entire trees that are left at the shoulder for collection.  Please work with the City in keeping these guidelines in mind when cleaning up your yard this fall.  If you have any questions, please call the Department of Public Works office at 618-662-4625.

Remember that weather may slow down the leaf picker.  The vacuum will not work if the leaves are extremely wet or if it is snowing.

title: GATEWAY CHANGES DISINFECTANT
full_story:
Beginning Monday, November 16th Gateway Regional Water Company will begin a modified disinfection process using Free Chlorine instead of Chloramines for its predominant water disinfectant.  Beginning December 21st, they will switch back from Free Chlorine residual to the normal Chloramines residual for its predominant water disinfectant.

Customers with health issues should contact their physicians with any health-related questions.

Customers on Gateway Regional Water Company include the City of Flora; Clay County Water; Western Wayne Water Company; Village of Xenia; Village of Iuka; City of Kinmundy; Village of Alma; Village of Farina; Fayette Water Company; FMC Water Co.; NEMC Water Co.; Village of Patoka; Raccoon Water Co.; and Village of Vernon.

If you have any questions, please contact Gateway at 618-775-1004.

title: DRIVE SOBER OR GET PULLED OVER
full_story:
The Illinois Department of Transportation, Illinois State Police and local law enforcement agencies across the state are putting a heightened focus on impaired driving this Halloween, reminding the public about the “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” and “Drive High, Get a DUI” safety campaigns, which run through this weekend.

“No one should ever drive under the influence of alcohol or drugs.  The only choice to make is to never get behind the wheel if you’re impaired,” said Stephane B. Seck-Birhame, bureau chief of Safety Programs and Engineering at IDOT.  “Remember — It’s Not a Game.’”

In addition to the heightened focus on impaired driving, the safety effort also reinforces the importance of seat belt use, adherence to the speed limit and other traffic laws.

“Whether you are headed to a Halloween party or simply driving like any other day, ISP reminds you of the four deadly driving behaviors; speeding, DUI, no seat belt and distracted driving,” said ISP Division of Patrol Col. Chris Owen.  “ISP will have extra patrols for the Halloween weekend and we’ll be looking for the Fatal Four.”

The “Drive Sober or Get Pulled Over” and “Drive High.  Get a DUI” campaigns, along with increased traffic enforcement, are funded by federal highway safety grants and administered by IDOT.  These efforts are supported by ISP and local law enforcement.  The campaigns are reinforced by IDOT’s “It’s Not a Game” initiative, which spotlights driving and highway safety throughout Illinois.
